quests.protocolRule: Think about what all three callers likely agree on.
quests.crisisScene: Three different callers report the same car crash, each giving a slightly different cross street. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: USE THE COMMON DETAILS TO CONFIRM ONE LOCATION
quests.actionGuidance: Comparing details across multiple callers helps identify the most likely accurate location, even if each report alone is imperfect.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether all three reports truly match each other.
quests.crisisScene: One of the three callers is actually describing a completely different, minor incident nearby. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEPARATE THAT CALL AS ITS OWN REPORT
quests.actionGuidance: Recognizing the mismatch prevents merging two separate incidents into one confused report.

quests.protocolRule: Do you wait for certainty?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a crash, but a friend at the scene keeps shouting a different location in the background. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND HELP TO THE MOST LIKELY LOCATION WHILE CONFIRMING WHICH IS RIGHT
quests.actionGuidance: Help can start moving while the location is confirmed, and crews can be redirected.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Think about what a dispatcher can teach someone to do right now, even untrained.
quests.crisisScene: A caller says her husband collapsed and isn't breathing, and she doesn't know what to do. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GUIDE HER THROUGH CHEST COMPRESSIONS STEP BY STEP
quests.actionGuidance: Talking a caller through chest compressions step by step can keep someone alive in the minutes before paramedics arrive.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what keeps compressions going if she can't continue alone.
quests.crisisScene: She says she's getting tired after a few minutes and isn't sure she can keep going. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ENCOURAGE HER AND ASK IF ANYONE ELSE CAN TAKE OVER
quests.actionGuidance: Encouragement and finding someone to switch in keeps compressions from stopping, which matters more than any one person's stamina.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what your role is once trained help physically arrives.
quests.crisisScene: Paramedics arrive and take over, confirming they'll handle it from here. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: THANK HER AND END THE GUIDANCE CALMLY
quests.actionGuidance: Once paramedics take over in person, phone guidance is no longer needed, and the call can end calmly.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what information still needs collecting, just typed instead of spoken.
quests.crisisScene: A caller using a text-based emergency service reports a break-in but can't speak on a voice call. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CONTINUE VIA TEXT AND GATHER KEY DETAILS THE SAME WAY
quests.actionGuidance: The same key details, location and situation, still need gathering, just exchanged through text instead of speech.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what keeps her hidden while still getting information out.
quests.crisisScene: The texting caller says the intruder is still inside and getting closer to the caller's hiding spot. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL HER TO STAY SILENT AND KEEP TEXTING QUIETLY
quests.actionGuidance: Texting quietly lets her keep communicating without making noise that could reveal her hiding spot to the intruder.

quests.protocolRule: What kind of question is easiest to answer fast?
quests.crisisScene: A texting caller sends only 'fire' and 'help' and then stops typing. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: TEXT BACK SHORT YES/NO QUESTIONS AND SEND FIREFIGHTERS WHILE GETTING THE ADDRESS
quests.actionGuidance: Yes/no questions are easy to answer under stress, and help shouldn't wait for the address.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what you can do the moment the line goes dead.
quests.crisisScene: A call about a serious injury suddenly disconnects mid-conversation. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL THE NUMBER BACK IMMEDIATELY
quests.actionGuidance: Calling back immediately can reconnect you to a caller who may still need urgent guidance or have new information.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what happens if you wait for the callback before sending help.
quests.crisisScene: The callback doesn't connect, but responders are already on the way based on the address given earlier. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND RESPONDERS ANYWAY, DON'T WAIT ON THE CALLBACK
quests.actionGuidance: Sending responders with the information already collected avoids delaying help just because a callback didn't connect.

quests.protocolRule: Should you wait for her to reconnect?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reporting a possible break-in at her house suddenly disconnects. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL BACK ONCE AND SEND POLICE TO THE ADDRESS ALREADY GIVEN
quests.actionGuidance: A disconnection during a break-in may mean danger, so police should go on the information already collected.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether it's your job to decide who's right here.
quests.crisisScene: Two witnesses to a fight give different descriptions of who started it. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT BOTH ACCOUNTS, LET OFFICERS SORT IT OUT
quests.actionGuidance: Passing along both accounts honestly lets trained officers investigate, rather than you deciding whose story to believe.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Ask what detail you can act on confidently, despite the conflict.
quests.crisisScene: Both witnesses agree on one key detail: one person is now bleeding from the head. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: PRIORITIZE THE INJURY THAT BOTH AGREE ON
quests.actionGuidance: A detail both witnesses agree on, like the head injury, is reliable enough to prioritize immediately, regardless of the other disagreement.

quests.protocolRule: Who decides how much weight it gets?
quests.crisisScene: A witness to a bar fight is certain about what she saw, but her friend says she's had several drinks. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT HER ACCOUNT AND NOTE THE UNCERTAINTY, LET POLICE ASSESS
quests.actionGuidance: Passing on the account and the doubt lets police weigh it without you deciding.

quests.protocolRule: Ask which version of events actually matches what's happening now.
quests.crisisScene: A caller first says her son 'just has a cold,' but then says he's actually struggling to breathe. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT THE BREATHING TROUBLE AS THE REAL PICTURE
quests.actionGuidance: The updated, more serious description should guide the response, since it reflects what's actually happening now.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what encourages honest reporting next time.
quests.crisisScene: She explains she downplayed it at first because she didn't want to overreact. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REASSURE HER THAT REPORTING IT WAS THE RIGHT CALL
quests.actionGuidance: Reassuring her that reporting accurately was correct encourages honest, complete information on future calls too.

quests.protocolRule: Which is more reliable: her words or the sound?
quests.crisisScene: A caller says her husband is 'fine', but you can hear him gasping in the background. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TRUST WHAT YOU HEAR AND TREAT IT AS A BREATHING EMERGENCY
quests.actionGuidance: Gasping is an objective sign of a breathing problem that her reassurance can't cancel.

quests.protocolRule: Think about how to be kind while still steering the call.
quests.crisisScene: During a real house fire, a panicked caller keeps mentioning an unrelated argument he had with his brother the day before. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: ACKNOWLEDGE HIM BRIEFLY AND REFOCUS ON THE FIRE
quests.actionGuidance: A brief acknowledgment shows you're listening, while refocusing keeps the call centered on the actual emergency.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what matters most now that you have real information.
quests.crisisScene: Once refocused, he clearly says his elderly mother is still inside on the second floor. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET THIS TO FIREFIGHTERS AS THE TOP PRIORITY
quests.actionGuidance: A trapped person's exact location is the single most urgent detail firefighters need, and it must reach them immediately.

quests.protocolRule: What could burning chemicals release?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reporting a fire mentions a chemical smell from a cabinet beside the flames. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE CHEMICALS TO FIREFIGHTERS IMMEDIATELY AND STAY OUT
quests.actionGuidance: Burning chemicals may release toxic fumes, which changes how firefighters approach.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what he needs to hear before he'll feel safe sharing.
quests.crisisScene: A witness to a crime is scared of retaliation and hesitant to give any identifying details. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REASSURE HIM AND EXPLAIN WHY DETAILS HELP SAFELY
quests.actionGuidance: Addressing his fear directly and explaining how the information helps makes him more likely to share useful details safely.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether pushing harder would help or backfire here.
quests.crisisScene: He then agrees to describe the suspect's clothing and direction of travel, but nothing more. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TAKE WHAT HE'S WILLING TO GIVE, DON'T PUSH FURTHER
quests.actionGuidance: Accepting what he's comfortable sharing still gives officers useful details, without risking him shutting down entirely.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Who can bridge the language gap?
quests.crisisScene: A witness to a crime is willing to talk but speaks a language the operator doesn't know. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CONNECT AN INTERPRETER AND KEEP THE QUESTIONS SIMPLE
quests.actionGuidance: An interpreter lets the witness be understood, and simple questions reduce errors.

quests.protocolRule: Think about the order: comfort first, then narrow down the vague phrase.
quests.crisisScene: A crying caller reports her elderly father 'isn't acting right' after a fall, without further detail. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALM HER, THEN ASK SPECIFIC QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS BEHAVIOR
quests.actionGuidance: Calming her first makes it possible to then ask clear questions that turn 'not acting right' into something responders can use.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what this specific combination of signs points to.
quests.crisisScene: She clarifies that he can't move his left arm and his speech sounds slurred. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR AN AMBULANCE, THIS MAY BE A STROKE
quests.actionGuidance: Slurred speech and an unmoving arm are classic stroke signs, so an ambulance should be called immediately once these are clear.

quests.protocolRule: How is he speaking and behaving?
quests.crisisScene: A different caller reports her father fell but is talking normally and just has a small bruise. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: ADVISE A DOCTOR'S VISIT IF ANYTHING CHANGES, NO AMBULANCE NEEDED
quests.actionGuidance: Normal speech and a small bruise suggest a minor fall. A doctor's visit is enough unless something changes.

quests.protocolRule: Think about the order that gets help moving fastest.
quests.crisisScene: A caller is sobbing, reports a car in a river with people inside, and keeps repeating herself without giving the location. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALM HER BRIEFLY, THEN GET THE EXACT LOCATION FIRST
quests.actionGuidance: A brief calming moment followed by getting the exact location gets rescuers moving immediately, even before every detail is known.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what changed about how many people rescuers need to focus on.
quests.crisisScene: She then says one person has gotten out and is on the riverbank, but another is still inside the sinking car. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT ONE PERSON SAFE AND ONE STILL TRAPPED
quests.actionGuidance: Clearly separating who's safe from who's still trapped lets rescuers focus their full effort on the person still in danger.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what's still useful about staying connected to her.
quests.crisisScene: Minutes later, she confirms rescuers have arrived and are entering the water toward the car. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: STAY ON THE LINE FOR ANY FURTHER UPDATES
quests.actionGuidance: Staying on the line means you can pass along any last-second changes rescuers might need as they carry out the rescue.
